text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Prices of Romanian-made cigarettes to rise by 60 percent in March.
- Electricity and gas price hikes go into effect this week.
- The foreign exchange market is confronted with a shortage of lei due to central bank measures to liberalise the interest rate for its weekly refinancing credits.
- People queue at bank offices to change their hard currency savings into lei and to put lei into bank deposits, taking advantage of higher rates offered.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Romgaz RA gas distribution authority cut gas supplies of food industry Carne Arad SA due to a 90.5 million lei outstanding bill.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Renel RA electricity authority raised $ 150 million through a corporate bond issue launched through Merill Lynch International.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The 1997 budget law will be presented to parliament in early March, Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea said.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- It is Hungary's interest that NATO should extend its borders to Romania's east, said Viktor Orban, chairman of Hungarian parliament's European integration commission after meeting with President Emil Constantinescu.
- Interviews with ethnic Romanian leaders from Ukraine and Moldova on the impact of the Romanian-Ukrainian treaty talks.
- Relatives of Gypsy King Ion Cioaba had Gypsy tradition prevail over hospital rules by removing Cioaba's body from the hospital a few hours after his death, rather than 24-hour interval.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The visit of Romania's exiled King Michael will be broadcast live on Romanian public television.
- Justice ministry official said that restoring exiled King Michael's Romanian citizenship does not involve returning his former properties.
- The opposition leftwing Party of Social Democracy said that it would oppose any propaganda aimed at rehabilitating the idea of monarchy in Romania.

- The Bishop of Arges said he would offer "only a glass of water" to former King Michael when he visits the Curtea de Arges monastery. "I should have been told, because we mortals communicate with each other. Only Jesus travels incognito."
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The Clinton Administration presented the report on NATO's expansion before the U.S.Congress.
-- Bucharest Newsroom, 40-1 3120264
